chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from 'Imran ibn Musa, from Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Al-Nu'man, from his father, from some of his men, who said:

A man came to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) and said, 'O Amir al-Mu'minin, I have been deprived of night prayer.' He said, and Amir al-Mu'minin said to him, 'You are a man whom your sins have bound/chained.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Title of Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: Why am I unable to perform night prayer?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) diagnoses the man's inability to perform night prayer not as a lack of opportunity, but as a spiritual consequence of his accumulated sins, which act as chains binding his heart. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of 'barrier of sin' (hijab al-dhunub), where major sins create a veil that hinders spiritual receptivity and the ease of worship. The Imam’s concise response underscores the causal link between moral conduct and spiritual capacity in Shi'i piety.
